messages:
zoe.design: Dropped a compact IA mock that groups nav by lifecycle: Build / Serve / Observe. Figma: https://figma.redwood/console/sideflow-v2
arjun.pm: looks cleaner. Big question: will moving 'Models' into Serve break saved links for customers?
mike.frontend: plan is to keep canonical paths and support aliases. middleware will detect legacy segments and either redirect or show a migration banner.
luca.platform: telemetry reqs: log alias hits with `legacy_segment`, `org_id_hash`, and timestamp. keep logs 45 days.
hana.a11y: a11y note: when we reorder or collapse groups, keyboard focus needs predictable placement. recommend setting focus to the nearest visible item and announce via aria-live: "Navigation updated, focus moved to <label>."
zoe.design: small correction — announce "Navigation updated: focus moved to <label>" and ensure group headers have `aria-expanded`.
mike.frontend: implementation details: add `data-legacy-path` attrs so middleware can map client-side too. show a subtle toast on redirect: "Old link redirected. Click to copy new URL."
arjun.pm: breadcrumbs — prefer resource hierarchy (Org > Workspace > Page). for quick actions use action chips next to crumbs.
hana.a11y: prefer U+203A for visual separator but mark separators aria-hidden. avoid relying on hash fragments for routing state.
luca.platform: rollout: internal dogfood -> 20% experiment -> full with 30d alias monitoring. we'll switch 302->301 after metrics look stable.
mike.frontend: dev tasks: alias table + middleware, banner + toast, aria-live announce, focus reconciliation. estimate 3 dev days + 1 QA.
arjun.pm: copy for banner: "You're viewing this page via a migration mapping. Update bookmark? [Copy link]"
links-bot: Created RED-9001: "Sideflow IA: grouping, alias redirects & breadcrumb contract" assigned to mike.frontend, luca.platform; due 2026-06-12.
